## CLAUDE CODE — Guardian-equivalent research (all pages verified against `scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv`; quotes from raw `.md` fetched via curl from `code.claude.com/docs/en/`)

### (1) Native judge mechanism: **YES — but unusable on our path**

Claude Code ships **auto mode**, an LLM-classifier safety reviewer that is architecturally the same thing as our Guardian.

`permission-modes.md` (§ "Eliminate permission prompts with auto mode"):
> "Auto mode lets Claude execute without routine permission prompts. A separate classifier model reviews actions before they run, blocking anything that escalates beyond your request, targets unrecognized infrastructure, or appears driven by hostile content Claude read. Explicit ask rules still force a prompt."

It even reviews inter-agent messages and root/home removals, and runs during plan mode ("the classifier reviews shell commands during planning instead of prompting you"). The SDK exposes it as a permission mode — `agent-sdk/permissions.md` mode table: "`auto` | Model-classified approvals | A model classifier approves or denies permission prompts. See Auto mode for availability".

**Why it does not cover claude-runtime:** availability is gated on first-party models and providers. `auto-mode-config.md`:
> "**Model**: on the Anthropic API and Claude Platform on AWS, Claude Opus 4.6 or later, Sonnet 4.6 or later, or Fable 5. ... Older models ... are not supported on any provider."
> "**Provider**: available by default on the Anthropic API, Claude Platform on AWS, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, and signed-in Claude apps gateway sessions."

Our claude-runtime runs the SDK against the Nessy gateway through the loopback Anthropic-Messages adapter with gateway models (`tgpt/qwen35-...`) — neither a listed provider nor a listed model, and the classifier issues its own model requests (`permission-modes.md`: a failure message "names a model and says auto mode 'cannot determine the safety' of an action means a classifier request failed"). So the native judge cannot fire on our stack.

### (2) Documented extension point for hosting OUR judge: **PreToolUse hook — and we already own it**

The docs are explicit that the hook layer is the one mechanism that gates every call in every mode, including `bypassPermissions`:

`agent-sdk/permissions.md` (§ "How permissions are evaluated", Step 1):
> "Run hooks first. A hook can deny the call outright or pass it on."

and (§ allowed_tools warning):
> "For checks that must run on every tool call, use a `PreToolUse` hook: hooks run before every other step, and a hook deny applies even in `bypassPermissions` mode."

The docs even warn that `canUseTool` is the WRONG place — it is shadowed by bypass: "Auto-approved tools never reach `canUseTool`. A tool call approved at any earlier step, by `acceptEdits` or `bypassPermissions`, or by an allow rule, skips your `canUseTool` callback" — and the SDK emits a `CLAUDE_SDK_CAN_USE_TOOL_SHADOWED` warning under `permissionMode: 'bypassPermissions'`, telling you: "To gate every tool call regardless of mode and rules, use a `PreToolUse` hook instead."

Hook decision contract, `agent-sdk/hooks.md`:
> "For `PreToolUse` hooks, this is where you set `permissionDecision` (`\"allow\"`, `\"deny\"`, `\"ask\"`, or `\"defer\"`), `permissionDecisionReason`, and `updatedInput`."

**What we pass today** (`/Users/i.i.gavrikov/Desktop/work/nessy-desktop/packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts`): the runtime already runs the SDK with `permissionMode: 'bypassPermissions'` (line 1457, comment: "Bypass SDK's built-in permission system - we handle all permissions via PreToolUse hook") and registers a single internal `PreToolUse` hook (line ~1469) that runs `runClaudePreToolUseHookPipeline` → `runPreToolUseChecks` — our own centralized permission pipeline. A Guardian call slots into that existing pipeline as one more check returning `permissionDecision: "deny"`/`"ask"`; no new SDK surface is needed.

### (3) What Claude Code itself does in bypassPermissions

Per `permission-modes.md` (§ "Skip all checks with bypassPermissions mode"): "`bypassPermissions` mode disables permission prompts and safety checks so tool calls execute immediately, including writes to protected paths." The documented residual guards are: explicit **ask rules** ("Explicit ask rules ... still prompt"), **deny rules** (`agent-sdk/permissions.md`: "If a deny rule matches, the tool is blocked, even in `bypassPermissions` mode"), hook denies (quote above), and two cross-session-messaging safeguards. The docs' own warning:
> "`bypassPermissions` offers no protection against prompt injection or unintended actions. For background safety checks with far fewer permission prompts, use auto mode instead."

I.e. Claude Code's documented answer to "autonomy without a human in the loop" is exactly a classifier judge (auto mode) — and where that isn't available, hooks/deny rules plus OS-level isolation (`sandboxing.md`: "you define which files and network domains commands can touch, and the operating system enforces that boundary for every Bash command and its child processes"; note Nessy's standing decision keeps sandbox OFF).

### (4) Verdict: **NEEDED — HOSTABLE-VIA-PreToolUse-hook**

- The harness HAS a native guardian-equivalent (auto mode's classifier), but its documented model/provider gates exclude our gateway-backed claude-runtime, so we cannot rely on it: on our path `bypassPermissions` runs with "no protection against prompt injection or unintended actions" beyond deny/ask rules.
- Our Guardian is therefore needed on claude-runtime, and the docs name the exact hosting point: a `PreToolUse` hook returning `permissionDecision` — the only step that "runs before every other step" and whose deny "applies even in `bypassPermissions` mode". `canUseTool` is documented as shadowed in our configuration and must not be used.
- Implementation cost is low: `claude-agent.ts` already owns the sole internal PreToolUse hook and a centralized check pipeline (`runPreToolUseChecks`); the judge becomes an additional check inside it, gated on the same permission bands as Pi.

Cited pages (all present in `scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv`): `agent-sdk/permissions`, `agent-sdk/hooks`, `permission-modes`, `auto-mode-config`, `hooks`, `sandboxing`.

## CODEX GUARDIAN — wire contract, config, docs, wiring cost, verdict

**Verdict: PRESENT, READY-TO-WIRE at the decision level; PARTIAL at the product level.** Codex ships a native server-side LLM judge ("Guardian" / Auto-review). It is a config knob, the judging runs entirely inside the codex app-server, and the client owes **no** wire answer — but the three wire messages that make it visible are `[UNSTABLE]`-marked, our adapter currently drops them silently, and two enablement details need a practice check against the pinned binary.

### 1. Wire contract (pinned `openai/codex rust-v0.147.0`, `packages/codex-protocol`)

**Server→client notifications (fire-and-forget; client responds to nothing):**

| Method | Payload type | Content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `item/autoApprovalReview/started` | `ItemGuardianApprovalReviewStartedNotification` | `threadId, turnId, startedAtMs, reviewId, targetItemId\|null, review, action` |
| `item/autoApprovalReview/completed` | `ItemGuardianApprovalReviewCompletedNotification` | same + `completedAtMs`, `decisionSource: AutoReviewDecisionSource` (sole member: `"agent"`) |
| `guardianWarning` | `GuardianWarningNotification` | `{threadId, message}` — "Concise guardian warning message for the user." (the denial circuit-breaker channel) |

- `GuardianApprovalReview` = `{status: "inProgress"|"approved"|"denied"|"timedOut"|"aborted", riskLevel: "low"|"medium"|"high"|"critical"|null, userAuthorization: "unknown"|"low"|"medium"|"high"|null, rationale: string|null}`. Docstring: "[UNSTABLE] Temporary approval auto-review payload … This shape is expected to change soon."
- `GuardianApprovalReviewAction` — 6 variants: `command`, `execve`, `applyPatch`, `networkAccess`, `mcpToolCall`, `requestPermissions` (files: `generated/v2/GuardianApprovalReviewAction.ts`).
- `targetItemId` is null for network-policy reviews (documented in the type's own comment).

**Client→server request (the only one):** `thread/approveGuardianDeniedAction` `{threadId, event: JsonValue}` → empty response. The `event` is a "Serialized `codex_protocol::protocol::GuardianAssessmentEvent`" — a v1-protocol blob that is NOT obviously derivable from the v2 notification payloads; this is the roughest edge (see cost sketch).

**Flow implication — who judges:** codex itself. The reviewer is a server-side subagent (`decisionSource: "agent"`); reviewer-eligible `item/*/requestApproval` server-requests simply stop arriving at the client and the notifications above arrive instead. The client's only optional verb is the post-denial override.

### 2. Config knobs (`packages/codex-protocol/schema/config-schema.json`)

- Root `approvals_reviewer`: enum `"user" | "auto_review" | "guardian_subagent"`. Schema: "Configures who approval requests are routed to for review. … Defaults to `user`. `auto_review` uses a carefully prompted subagent to gather relevant context and apply a risk-based decision framework before approving or denying the request. The legacy value `guardian_subagent` is accepted for compatibility."
- `[auto_review].policy` (`AutoReviewToml`): "Additional policy instructions inserted into the guardian prompt." (Note: the docs page says both `[auto_review].policy` and `guardian_policy_config` **replace** the reviewer policy — schema wording and doc wording disagree; trust the doc's "replace" for planning.)
- `features.guardian_approval`, `features.guardianv2`, `features.exec_permission_approvals` — bare booleans, **no descriptions** in the schema; whether 0.147.0 gates the v2 notifications behind `guardianv2` is unverified (practice check against the pinned binary needed).
- Per-profile (`ConfigProfile.approvals_reviewer`), per-app (`AppConfig.approvals_reviewer`), and managed-enterprise (`allowed_approvals_reviewers`, `guardian_policy_config`) overrides exist.
- **First-class per-thread field**: `thread/start` params include `approvalsReviewer?: ApprovalsReviewer | null` (`schema/v2/ThreadStartParams.json`) — enabling needs no TOML rewrite and no respawn.

**What we set today:** `buildCodexConfigToml` (`packages/codex-responses-adapter/src/config-writer.ts:555`) emits `model`, `model_provider`, `web_search`, `approval_policy`, `sandbox_mode`, permissions profile, shell-env policy, MCP servers — **never** `approvals_reviewer`, `[auto_review]`, or any `features.*`. `codex-agent.ts:341` sends `thread/start` with only `{cwd, model}`. So guardian is at its default `user` in every Nessy build.

**What we handle today: nothing.** `packages/shared/src/agent/backend/codex/event-adapter.ts` has a `default: return []` — all three guardian notifications are silently dropped. `isApprovalMethod` (`packages/codex-agent-server/src/approval-bridge.ts:618`) bridges the 6 requestApproval/elicitation methods only; `thread/approveGuardianDeniedAction` is never sent. Repo grep confirms zero guardian handling outside `codex-protocol` (all other "guardian" hits are Nessy's own Pi guardian-judge-core).

### 3. Docs (raw curl quotes)

Contract pages (both fetched raw, greps verbatim):
- `https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/sandboxing/auto-review.md` — the full lifecycle page: "Auto-review replaces manual approval at the sandbox boundary with a separate reviewer agent."; "Auto-review only applies when approvals are interactive. In practice, that means `approval_policy = \"on-request\"` or a granular approval policy…"; "With `approval_policy = \"never\"`, there is nothing to review."; "Prompt-build, review-session, and parse failures fail closed."; "Auto-review interrupts the turn after `3` consecutive denials or `10` denials within a rolling window of the last `50` reviews in the same turn."; "The reviewer is itself a Codex agent"; override: "run `/approve` to open the **Auto-review Denials** picker … it applies to the exact denied action … recorded for one retry in the same context; and the retry still goes through Auto-review."
- `https://developers.openai.com/codex/sandbox.md` § "Automatic approval reviews": "Set `approvals_reviewer = \"auto_review\"` to route eligible approval requests through a reviewer agent before Codex runs the request"; "The reviewer policy checks for data exfiltration, credential probing, persistent security weakening, and destructive actions."; "Automatic review uses extra model calls, so it can add to Codex usage."
- `https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks.md` and `https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/plugins.md`: **zero** guardian/auto-review mentions (grepped the fetched files).
- Practice, not contract: default policy text lives at `github.com/openai/codex` `codex-rs/core/src/guardian/policy.md` / `policy_template.md`.

### 4. Cost sketch — enable native vs host ours

**Enable codex's native guardian (small):**
1. One line: add `approvalsReviewer: 'auto_review'` to the `thread/start` params in `codex-agent.ts:341` (band-conditional: Nessy auto/bypass bands only), or emit `approvals_reviewer` from `buildCodexConfigToml`. Optionally `[auto_review]` policy text carrying Nessy's own judge policy (doc warns it REPLACES the default — paste-complete-policy-first rule).
2. Visibility (required for product honesty): add `item/autoApprovalReview/started|completed` + `guardianWarning` cases to `event-adapter.ts` → render a review item with status/riskLevel/rationale. Without this the judge runs invisibly.
3. Optional override UX: `thread/approveGuardianDeniedAction` — blocked on figuring out where the serialized `GuardianAssessmentEvent` comes from on the v2 surface (practice check in openai/codex needed; it is not in the v2 notification payloads).
4. Verify on the pinned 0.147.0 binary: (a) whether `features.guardianv2`/`guardian_approval` must be set; (b) that the reviewer subagent's model calls route through our `model_provider` (the Nestor responses adapter) — "extra model calls" through the gateway is both a cost and a dependency; a reviewer hardwired to OpenAI backends would fail closed on every review in our build ("Prompt-build, review-session, and parse failures fail closed" — i.e. everything denied).
5. Semantics shift to accept knowingly: reviewer-eligible approvals stop reaching our approval bridge, so codex's judge REPLACES the Nessy permission card for those actions in whatever band enables it; and in bands mapped to `approval_policy = "never"` (our unattended mode) there is nothing to review — same trigger limit as Pi's guardian bands.

**Host OUR judge instead (also cheap, different shape):** every boundary-crossing action already arrives at `handleServerRequest` (`codex-agent.ts:451`) as a requestApproval; inserting a `guardian-judge-core` consult there before surfacing/auto-approving needs no protocol or config change and keeps one judge/policy across all three runtimes — but it sees exactly the same trigger set (escalations only), judges with less context than codex's reviewer (which reads the transcript server-side), and gets none of codex's denial circuit breaker.

Key files: `packages/codex-protocol/generated/v2/Guardian*.ts`, `packages/codex-protocol/generated/ServerNotification.ts:79`, `packages/codex-protocol/generated/ClientRequest.ts:99`, `packages/codex-protocol/schema/config-schema.json`, `packages/codex-responses-adapter/src/config-writer.ts:555`, `packages/shared/src/agent/codex-agent.ts:341,451`, `packages/shared/src/agent/backend/codex/event-adapter.ts:287`, `packages/codex-agent-server/src/approval-bridge.ts:618`.
